stage: Task 2 executable user-assumption baseline and sensitivity
guardrails: User cost points are rounded scenario choices, not exact midpoints or complete initial capital estimates. Historical source scope/price flags are unchanged.
Relative ridership 1 vs 1.2 is a user hypothesis. Do not invent daily totals, forecast horizons or infer demand from capacity.
Surface LRT is not automatically grade-separated. Fifteen signals and 2.5/3.5 minutes are assumptions; the 10/14-second-per-signal equivalents are arithmetic, not observed target performance.
Cost per km is diagnostic only. E=R/C overlaps with explicitly scored R; the inverse-cost view tests this issue.
Weight shares explore a declared Dirichlet prior with fixed inputs, not statistical confidence or probability of project success.
Normalization and preference changes switch the winner. Do not call BRT a robust final technology recommendation.
A verified hard failure still overrides provisional admission. Preserve capital ceiling, full nine-year delivery/deadline, route and depot conditions and all Task 1 data.
next_tasks: Reconcile complete initial capital and comparable price/cash-flow basis for BRT/LRT, with consultant exclusions and no duplicate components.
Develop project-start-to-operational schedules with property/utilities, approvals/design/procurement, fleet/depot, tests and justified overlap.
Obtain matched Finch East travel-time/demand evidence and full-route/depot strategies; replace assumptions explicitly with documented estimates.
Rerun the existing normalization, efficiency-definition and weight sensitivity; resolve final feasibility before making an implementation recommendation.
